subject: Clarify invoice discrepancy: aggregation vs per-call rounding
messages:
From: Markus Hanke <markus@brighthealth.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discrepancy on Dec invoice — aggregation math

Hi Priyom,

We received the December invoice and there are two line items that don't reconcile with our usage dashboard. Specifically:
- Nov 28–Dec 1: multiple short chat calls where our dashboard shows 4,200 input tokens and 3,800 output tokens; invoice shows charge for 9,000 tokens.
- Several streaming calls on Dec 1 show the same session_id but were billed as separate calls (invoice treated them as rounded to full-minimum each).

Can you explain: 1) whether you aggregate tokens across calls in a session for billing, 2) how rounding/minimums are applied (per-call vs per-session), and 3) whether KV/prefix cache reuse is credited on subsequent calls? I've attached the invoice extract.

We want to avoid repeating misunderstandings during renewal conversations. If there's a clear offset we can agree on a one-time adjustment.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Platform
BrightHealth AI

--

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Dec invoice — aggregation math

Hi Markus — thanks for the details and the sample invoice. Quick summary before a deeper pass: we do batch billing at the request-level but support session-level aggregation for long-lived conversational sessions when the customer enables "conversation rollup". Two things likely at play here: rounding minimums and whether the requests in question were tagged to the same conversation id (our system will only roll up tokens when the SDK populates the session/conversation metadata).

Short answers: 
- Aggregation: by default we bill per-request; customers can opt into conversation rollup which sums tokens across a conversation window (configurable, typically 1–24 hours). If rollup is off, each request is subject to the per-call minimum.
- Rounding/minimums: we apply a per-request billing quantum of 50 tokens for streaming and 10 tokens for non-streaming text requests, rounded up to the nearest quantum. For negotiated accounts (like BrightHealth), we can override quantums in the contract (and we do for RDW-4782 at the committed tier).
- KV/prefix cache: when the runtime detects a KV hit (same model variant + warm cache), the returned tokens are still billable but we credit repeated prefix tokens when cache reuse avoids re-encoding. Credits are applied as negative line items and show up as "KV reuse credit" on the invoice when triggered.

I've looped in Kar (karthik_iyer) and Vanessa to confirm whether the calls in your spreadsheet were captured with conversation ids and whether our billing pipeline emitted a KV credit. I'll follow up with an itemized breakdown and proposed adjustment if we find a mis-billing.

Propose: 1) we'll audit the invoice ranges you attached, 2) provide a short calculation showing the rounding points that caused the delta, and 3) if applicable, apply a one-time credit and include wording in the SOW amendment to ensure rollup behavior is explicit.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Dec invoice — aggregation math

Markus — follow-up after the pipeline audit. Summary of findings and proposal: 

1) Root cause: three streaming requests on Nov 30 were tagged with different ephemeral session ids (client-side library restarted between requests). Because conversation rollup was not triggered, each request hit the per-request streaming quantum (50 tokens). The raw tokens add up to ~8,000 but after rounding they billed ~9,000 — that matches your invoice sample.

2) Contract quantum: I confirmed RDW-4782 reduces the streaming quantum to 25 tokens for your committed tier; the billing pipeline had an outdated config for a short window on Nov 30 while we pushed the new quantum rules to the staging pipeline. That's on us.

3) KV credits: no KV reuse credit was applied for those calls because they used different session ids and the prefix encoding path was re-run.

Proposed remediation:
- One-time credit: we'll issue a credit of the delta (invoice overcharge of 1,020 billable tokens → credit amount $204 at your unit price) and apply it to the Dec invoice.
- SOW amendment: attach the draft SOW that enumerates rollup window (24 hours default), required session-id instrumentation, negotiated quantums (streaming=25, non-streaming=10), and the KV credit rules. If that reads OK, we'll route the SOW via DocuSign and include the credit as an invoice-level line item.
- Engineering follow-up: Vanessa will coordinate a short checklist your engineers can add to ensure conversation ids persist across reconnects. Kar will validate pipeline config deploy process to prevent future staging mismatches.

Attachments: SOW_BrightHealth_draft_v1.docx (SOW draft), redwood_bill_explain_20261207.pdf (detailed calcs).

If you'd like, I can also propose a 3-month monitoring window where we run a side-by-side usage check and proactively flag any rounding anomalies before billing.

Thanks — and apologies for the noise.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
